research_scope: Five complete source-free reviews in closure, boundary, set accumulation and sequence accumulation. No new definitions, external mathematical source use or automatic aliases.

amendments.review_rationale: Examined the complete independently sourced closure, boundary or accumulation-point formulation and all previous mathematical dependency references; distinguished underlying set and sequence constructions from each formulation's own defining clause, preserving every previously classified occurrence and exact source version.

references.context: General topology: closed subset F⊆X in topology τ, characterized by X\F∈τ; no metric or Hausdorff assumptions.
references.reason: Closedness is a reusable prerequisite to taking the closure of an arbitrary subset A.
references.matching_note: Distinguish topologically closed subsets from Zariski closed subschemes.

references.phrase: intersection of all closed supersets of A
references.context: Set theory: arbitrary indexed intersection ⋂_{F∈𝔽}F of subsets of X, here 𝔽 comprises the closed F containing A; identifying this intersection with cl_X(A) is the definition of closure.
references.reason: Arbitrary intersection of an indexed family is a reusable set construction independent of the particular closure formula.
references.matching_note: The original raw phrase combines a set operation and its special closure family; inspect for compound-reference splitting in global audit.

references.disposition: The intersection remains closed and contains A; no arbitrary extrinsic universe is used.

references.phrase: family of closed supersets of A
references.disposition: The comprehension of all closed F⊆X containing A specifies the collection used to characterize this closure; the general closed-subset predicate is separately recorded in a sibling formulation.
Being contained in every closed superset of A is precisely the universal property defining closure; it is stronger than mere minimality and does not presuppose closure as a separate input.
Closure is contained in each closed superset, not merely one of many minimal elements.

references.context: Set theory: complement of A relative to its explicitly fixed ambient X, X\A={x∈X:x∉A}; both closures in the boundary formula are taken in X.
references.reason: Relative complement is a reusable set operation distinct from the particular boundary formula.
references.matching_note: Compare with recorded A\B difference candidate, preserving the ambient universe.

references.context: Set theory: binary intersection B∩C of subsets of X, applied to the two topological closures B=cl_X(A), C=cl_X(X\A); equality with the boundary is the definition of the current meaning.
references.reason: Binary set intersection is an independently reusable operation even when its inputs are closures.
references.matching_note: Compare contextually with general finite and arbitrary intersections at global alias stage.

references.disposition: Both formulas represent same boundary because complement of interior A is closure of complement.

references.context: Set theory: deletion A\{x} of singleton {x} from a set A, whether or not x belongs to A; a specialized relative set complement.
references.reason: Deleting a point is a reusable operation preceding the closure criterion for a set accumulation point.
references.matching_note: Do not equate accumulation of image sets with repeated visits of a sequence.

references.disposition: The universal statement that all open neighborhoods of x intersect the deleted set is precisely the defining accumulation-point criterion, not an additional prerequisite meaning.

references.phrase: set-accumulation distinct from sequence index accumulation
references.disposition: Requires distinct spatial points rather than infinitely many repeated visits.

references.context: Topological set theory: sequence as a map ℕ→X, n↦x_n, with possible repetition of values; counting visits uses distinct natural-number indices.
references.reason: An indexed sequence is a separate notion from its unordered image subset in X.
references.matching_note: Keep sequence, subsequence, net and image set distinct.

references.context: Set theory: infinite subset {n∈ℕ:x_n∈U} of natural-number indices, containing infinitely many distinct indices even if only one value is repeated in U; required for each open U containing x.
references.reason: Infinitude of a set of indices is a reusable cardinality predicate, while requiring it for every neighborhood defines accumulation of a sequence.
references.matching_note: Not equivalent to an infinite set of distinct spatial points.

references.disposition: Repeated sequence values count at distinct indices, unlike set accumulation definition.
